parsed.rationale: Both `PlaybackController` (line 27) and `AudioPlayerProtocol` (line 19) live in the same package (`Playback`) and the same directory (`Shared/Playback/Sources/PlaybackCore/Protocols/`), and they share five structurally identical members: `installRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `removeRenderTap:()`, and a `state` property (typed differently — `PlaybackState` vs `PlayerState` — which itself suggests a type-alignment opportunity). Extracting these shared members into a new parent protocol `AudioPlaybackCore` eliminates the duplication and makes the layering explicit: `AudioPlayerProtocol` is the lower-level engine contract, while `PlaybackController` adds higher-level concerns (`play:(reason:)`, `stop:(reason:)`, `toggle:(reason:)`, `isLoading`, `stateStream`). Neither record is a test, mock, codegen artefact, or sample-app file, so the duplication is not intentional by policy.
